quotes.text: The rapid growth and expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to revolutionize many sectors of American life but also brings new challenges. [...] Bad actors utilize AI or even a zealous AI system has the potential to disrupt markets in ways that we have not even fathomed yet.

AI has the potential to significantly impact our financial system and our capital markets and our banking system, and this needs to be addressed at every level on how we can mitigate against some of the negative consequences.

On the morning of May 22nd of this year, an AI-generated image of an explosion near the Pentagon spread widely throughout social media. Immediately, the stock market dipped, and we saw a significant decline. We were able to recover when we were able to confirm that it was, in fact, fake, but we know that these are challenges that we are going to have to address together.

Artificial intelligence will only become more advanced and available to scammers, and our policies need to keep up.

In my remaining time, I want to focus on the risks of artificial intelligence (AI) in the banking sector. [...] This is why I introduced the Preventing Deep Fake Scams Act with my friend and member of this committee, Congressman Mike Flood. This bill will establish a task force to examine AI in the financial services sector, including both the potential benefits of the technology for financial institutions and the unique risks it poses to customer account security.

I have significant concerns regarding the use of artificial intelligence in the banking sector. [...] This is why I introduced the Preventing Deep Fake Scams Act with my friend and colleague Rep. Mike Flood. This bill would set up a federal task force to engage with industry and examine how artificial intelligence is used in the banking sector and how we can best ensure that consumers are not harmed in the banking industry.

As artificial intelligence continues to rapidly advance and become more widely available, we’re just beginning to see the impacts on everything from our election systems with the use of deep fakes, to bank fraud perpetuated by the use of high-tech scams. Our policies must keep up to protect our financial system, American consumers, and our country at-large.

As AI continues to rapidly advance, it poses a threat to our elections, financial systems, and country at-large.

I really worry about areas like this where we need to be leading the way globally and making sure that China is not the one doing that. I don’t want a future where China’s leading on AI. It needs to be the United States and we have to come together in Congress to bring comprehensive pragmatic, bipartisan solutions.

China is making significant investments. We can’t get behind them, and this is really going to define, you know, what the next 100 years looks like for global leadership, and we need to make sure that it’s people here in the United States that are benefitting not only from these technologies in their lives, but also the financial benefit of innovating and leading here in the U.S.A.

Big tech shouldn't be allowed to use your data to make you pay more.

I signed on to @RepCasar and @RepRashida's Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act that would ban companies from looking at your browsing history, location, or demographics to charge you more or pay you less. You deserve fair prices – not more corporate tracking and price gouging.

This is deeply disturbing, but not the first warning sign.

Last Congress, I sat on a bipartisan AI task force created to make real progress ensuring AI developments prioritize our safety, well-being, and labor force. At the beginning of this Congress, Speaker Johnson unfortunately disregarded the Task Force's recommendations, and disbanded it.

We don’t have time to keep waiting. Congress must start the real work of putting up commonsense guardrails to avoid the worst outcomes these whistleblower are warning us of.

That’s why I just became a cosponsor of the Power for the People Act — a brand new bill to set commonsense guardrails on data center development, including water usage, environmental protections, and energy costs.

As AI continues to advance, we need commonsense guardrails to keep the public safe.

That starts with independent audits, making sure federal agencies have the funding & expertise to oversee these systems, and ensuring any AI that fails safety checks cannot be deployed in the U.S. New Tech should empower people, not put them at risk. It's up to us to make sure that stays at the center of innovation.

I'm proud this is my 6th bill passed into law this Congress — proving you can stand strong against this administration and still get important work done.

I’ve traveled to every corner of Colorado’s Seventh throughout this campaign. And no matter where I go — Lakewood, Leadville, Cañon City, and everywhere in between — the one thing everyone tells me they’re concerned about is data centers. And I share the concerns.
We need to have oversight of AI technologies. We need to have independent audits. We need to ensure that the technologies that they’re releasing are not a danger to our country.
It’s absolutely possible to take on as long as we have the right leadership and willingness to do so. And it couldn’t be more urgent.
